title: About
text:
I am an undergraduate student at the University of Toledo working toward bachelor’s degrees in Data Science and Disability Studies. I expect to graduate in May 2026. I am excited to apply my knowledge and skills to tackle real-world problems with creativity, curiosity, and a committment to making a meaningful impact.

Data Science Intern, U.S. Department of Education (September 2023-Present)

Cleaned and analyzed grant funding data using R (dplyr, tidyverse) in RStudio and Python (pandas, numpy) in Visual Studio Code. Utilized R markdown and Jupyter notebooks for organization and documentation of code.
Visualized data on grant funding by the National Center for Special Education Research using Python (seaborn, matplotlib) and Looker Studio.
Collaborated in a team-oriented environment on data science tasks, demonstrating flexibility and good judgement.



Research Assistant, University of Toledo (May 2022-August 2022)

Analyzed focus group data using qualitative methods and presented preliminary findings to project team members.
Conceptualized cognitive accessibility in website design, qualitative analysis, and accessible writing in Plain Language.

I love to be creative and make arts and crafts in my free time. I am an abstract artist, primarily working with watercolors. I also crochet.
I am deeply passionate about disability justice and promoting accessibility in our world.
